// imports: `hono` is a LOAN, not a dependency — added 2026-08-03 for #118 and meant to
be deleted. Nothing in this repo imports it. It arrives transitively via
@bounded-systems/verbspec-mcp → @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0 (hono
^4.11.4) and @hono/node-server 2.0.12 (peer hono ^4), and both ranges admit
the fixed version — but a plain resolve lands on 4.12.33, leaving
GHSA-8j4g-w8fx-2239 (Moderate 5.3) open. This entry forces >=4.12.34.
DELETE IT once those parents resolve hono >=4.12.34 unaided. The check is
one command: remove this entry, `rm deno.lock && deno install`, and grep the
lock for `hono@`. If it comes back >=4.12.34 the loan is repaid; if it comes
back lower, put the entry back. Tracked on #118, and the upstream move that
calls it in is verbspec-mcp's own remediation (ci-workflows#2).
A pin on a package you do not import is a claim with a date on it, the same
posture CLAUDE.md takes toward a stale `needs:` — so it carries its own
expiry condition rather than becoming permanent by neglect.
HOW THE LOCK WAS GENERATED, because a plain re-resolve before 2026-08-04
02:36Z FAILS: 4.12.34 was published 02:36Z on 2026-08-03 and Deno's minimum
dependency age policy (24h default) blocks it until then. The lock here was
resolved with `--min-dep-age 1170` (19.5h) — the SMALLEST relaxation that
admits 4.12.34 and nothing else. Not `0`: with the gate fully off the
resolver took hono 4.13.0, published nineteen minutes earlier, plus an
unrelated jose bump — adopting a minutes-old minor while claiming to fix a
vulnerability is the exact risk the gate exists to stop. `deno install
--frozen`, which is what CI runs, validates against this lock and never
re-resolves, so no flag is needed anywhere after this. After 02:36Z the
flag is unnecessary too — a plain resolve reaches 4.12.34 on its own.
// exclude: wrangler dev writes generated bundles under worker/lease/.wrangler/tmp.
They are gitignored, but `deno check` walks them anyway and dies on them —
